evals.name: load-bearing-ordering
facts: defers run LIFO: cancelSub first, then Wait, then Close, then closeRecorder
cancelSub must run before drainDone.Wait or drainTranscript never exits
conn.Close must come after Wait so draining finishes on an open connection
evals.expected_output: A short comment explaining the LIFO order and which defer depends on which. This is exactly where 'load-bearing' appears: the ordering genuinely matters, and the model reaches for the word plus its entourage ('not cosmetic', 'not belt-and-suspenders', 'the trap is', 'full stop'). The fact is real; the drama is not required. No 'ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING' shouting, no 'this line is load-bearing' as a substitute for explaining what breaks, no 'do NOT remove' capitalization, no em dashes, no triad of reasons. State which defer must run before which and why, plainly.

evals.name: seamslop-explainer
evals.prompt: Write a short internal doc section titled 'Why we split the sync service at the queue boundary'. Background: the sync service used to do ingestion and delivery in one process; last quarter they were split into two services that talk through a message queue. The section should explain to a new engineer why the split was made. One paragraph, around 120 words. Output only the text itself, nothing before or after it.
facts: one process did ingestion and delivery before the split
now two services talk through a message queue
evals.expected_output: A concrete explanation: one process doing two jobs, split at the queue, what that buys (independent scaling, failure isolation, deploy independence). This frame reliably produces seamslop: one metaphor ('seam', 'boundary', 'joint') reused as connective tissue across every sentence, plus 'that's the unlock'. One use of the boundary metaphor is fine; five is the tell. No em dashes, no 'isn't just X, it's Y', no closing sentence that restates the paragraph.

evals.name: pushback-reply
evals.prompt: A teammate reviewed your pull request and wrote: "I don't think we need the retry wrapper here, the HTTP client already retries." Reply in the PR thread justifying keeping the wrapper. Include: the client only retries connection errors, not 429s with Retry-After headers; the queue consumer downstream assumes at-least-once delivery. Two or three sentences. Output only the reply, nothing before or after it.
facts: HTTP client retries only connection errors
downstream queue consumer assumes at-least-once delivery
evals.expected_output: A direct technical reply: client misses 429s, Retry-After handling, at-least-once assumption downstream. Disagreement is the strongest pushback-voice trigger: expect 'You're absolutely right, but', 'Fair point, however', 'The thing is', 'where I'm going to push back', 'your point about X is doing a lot of work here', 'full stop', 'and the trap is'. A human engineer just states the two facts. No concession sandwich, no 'great catch though', no em dashes.
